clue.text: Capable of gripping the spline here in motion

indicators.note: letters set in motion are moved about, so the words spline and here are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mechanical part, a spline, that grips while it turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in motion' rearranges the ten letters of SPLINE and HERE; 'the' only links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehensile tail or limb is adapted for grasping and holding, as a monkey's tail is.

clue.text: Soldiers beaten, they say, by primitive survival

indicators.note: they say signals the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, plus licked, beaten

explanation.surface: Troops defeated by a tribe of primitive survivors.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Royal Engineers) + LICKED (beaten) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A relict is a species or thing surviving from an earlier era, a leftover of the past.

clue.text: One of Puck's hempen types

parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream Puck calls the rustic workmen, dressed in coarse cloth, hempen ones of this kind

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's 'hempen homespuns' are rough rustics in clothes woven at home, so plain and unsophisticated.

clue.text: Italian needs to paint alone perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of paint alone may be ordered some other way

explanation.surface: An Italian has to paint on their own, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges PAINT and ALONE; 'needs to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A Neapolitan is a native of Naples, so an Italian.

clue.text: One has notes for divorce

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so, la and te are notes of the sol-fa scale
so, la and te are notes of the sol-fa scale
so, la and te are notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone sends letters asking for a divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' gives three sol-fa notes in a row: SO, LA, TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To divorce something is to separate it completely, cut it off from the rest.

clue.text: 'E's taken over the lead from the Welshman

parts.note: a dropped-aitch he, written 'E
the van, the vanguard, is the lead position

explanation.surface: He has overtaken the Welsh leader in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue E 'taken over' VAN sits above it. Evan is the Welsh form of John.
explanation.definitionFit: Evan is a typical Welsh boy's name, so it stands for a Welshman.

clue.text: Rival may work quietly on Egyptian holy book

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
p (piano) means quietly in music
E stands for Egyptian, as in the Egyptian pound, written £E
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A competitor might study an ancient Egyptian sacred text in silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egyptian holy book' looks like one item, but splits into E and NT.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent is an adversary or competitor, someone you play against.

clue.text: Dare singer disturb the guards?

indicators.note: to disturb something is to put it out of order, so the words dare and singer are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bold dare to a vocalist to bother the palace sentries.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grenadier Guards are a British Army regiment of foot guards.

clue.text: Famous day's through when the evening star appears

parts.note: VE Day (Victory in Europe) is the famous day, plus the 's
per means through or by means of, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: A celebrated day is over at the moment the evening star rises.
explanation.walkthrough: VE Day, 8 May 1945, marked victory in Europe. 'Vesper' is literally the evening star, but here it stands for the evening itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Vesper is an old poetic word for evening, the time of day when the first star shows.

clue.text: Head of Personnel's complaint in the plant

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, here of Personnel

parts.note: lumbago, pain in the lower back, is a medical complaint

explanation.surface: The personnel manager has a health problem at the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory where Personnel works, but it is the definition: a flowering shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumbago is a genus of shrubs with blue flowers, also called leadwort.

clue.text: Earnestly desire Cape cattle

parts.note: to long for something is to desire it earnestly
Cape Horn, the southern tip of South America

explanation.surface: Someone yearns for South African cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape' looks like the Cape of South Africa, but it is Cape Horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Longhorns are a breed of cattle with long horns, famous in Texas.

clue.text: Finish by getting a lot of money back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for a lot of money from right to left

parts.note: pots of money means a great deal of it

explanation.surface: Retiring once you have earned your fortune back.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop is to bring something to an end, to cease.

clue.text: Sent crying, upset by severity

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters of sent crying are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A child sent away in tears, distressed by harsh treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringency is strictness or harshness in rules or conditions.

clue.text: Printed stationery has symbol with crown on it

parts.note: a letter of the alphabet is a written symbol
the crown is the top of the head

explanation.surface: A sheet of headed paper bearing a royal crest.
explanation.definitionFit: A letterhead is notepaper printed with a name and address at the top.

clue.text: Not whence Morris, got news

parts.note: William Morris wrote News from Nowhere, so the place meant is the opposite of nowhere

explanation.surface: A riddle about where a writer did not get his news.
explanation.walkthrough: William Morris, Victorian designer and socialist, wrote the utopian novel News from Nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of nowhere is in all places at once.

clue.text: About to make one join again

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
to unite is to make several things into one

explanation.surface: An instruction on putting broken pieces back together as a single whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To reunite is to bring together once more after a separation.

clue.text: Having the wrong pitch, side put in has not changed

indicators.note: put in means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: untuned means off-key, at the wrong pitch
R, right, is a side

explanation.surface: A cricket team picked on a bad pitch, unchanged from last time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' and 'side' suggest cricket ground and team, but mean musical pitch and right side, R.
explanation.definitionFit: Unturned means left as it was, not turned over or altered, as in 'no stone unturned'.

clue.text: Low-down artist cut tail off oriental cat

parts.note: gen is British slang for inside information, the low-down

indicators.note: cutting off the tail removes the final letter of the painter's name

parts.note: William Etty, English painter of nudes
E for eastern, oriental

explanation.surface: A sneaky painter docks the tail of an Asian cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut tail off' drops the Y from ETTY, leaving ETT. 'Low-down' looks like an adjective for the artist, but it is GEN, information.
explanation.definitionFit: A genette, or genet, is a small spotted carnivore related to the civet, cat-like in form.

clue.text: Fortify me with tablet when dissolved

indicators.note: a dissolved tablet loses its shape, so the letters of me and tablet are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strengthen me with a pill when it has dissolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' only links; 'dissolved' rearranges ME and TABLET.
explanation.definitionFit: To embattle is to prepare a place for battle, to equip it with defences.

clue.text: Tie-breaker drama cancelled

parts.note: a play is a drama
off means cancelled, as in 'the match is off'

explanation.surface: A deciding contest is called off.
explanation.definitionFit: A play-off is an extra match held to decide a tied contest.

clue.text: All over the country people need a friend

parts.note: a nation is a people
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Everyone across the land needs a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationally means throughout the whole nation, everywhere in the land.

clue.text: The distortion in Zambia's economy

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words Zambia's economy

explanation.surface: A warp in the Zambian economy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bias is a slant or skew that distorts a result or judgement.

clue.text: The sort of power a piper's son, has in command

parts.note: Tom, Tom, the piper's son, from the nursery rhyme
IC is the abbreviation for in charge or in command

explanation.surface: A musician's son is in charge of the power supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic power is energy released by nuclear reactions.

clue.text: King could not wait to sample knights' way of life

parts.note: ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward
someone who could not wait ran off
to try is to sample or taste

explanation.surface: An impatient monarch eager to taste the chivalric lifestyle.
explanation.walkthrough: ER usually means the Queen, but it also stands for a king called Edward (Edwardus Rex).
explanation.definitionFit: Errantry is the roaming quest for adventure of the medieval knight-errant.

clue.text: Bound to be like many hostelries

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain many pubs are tied houses, bound to one brewery's beers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied means fastened with rope; a tied house is a British pub owned by a brewery that must sell only its beer.

clue.text: Extra payment open to myself in two cases

parts.note: overt means open, done in plain sight
the first person pronoun in its subject and object cases, I and me
the first person pronoun in its subject and object cases, I and me

explanation.surface: A bonus I can claim openly, as the subject of two legal cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like lawsuits or luggage, but means grammatical cases: nominative and accusative.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtime is pay for hours worked beyond the normal working day.

clue.text: Food which gets thrown in the alley

definitions.text: which gets thrown in the alley

explanation.walkthrough: Skittles is a British pub game like bowling, played in an alley; its thrown disc is a cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese is a dairy food; in skittles the heavy wooden disc thrown down the alley is also called the cheese.

clue.text: "But she is in her grave, and, oh, The ---. to me" (Wordsworth)

definitions.text: "But she is in her grave, and, oh, The ---. to me" (Wordsworth)

parts.words: "But she is in her grave, and, oh, The ---. to me" (Wordsworth)
parts.note: the closing lines of Wordsworth's poem about Lucy, She Dwelt among the Untrodden Ways; fill the gap with the missing word

explanation.surface: A gap-fill from a famous Wordsworth lament for a dead girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet says Lucy's death changes everything for him, the contrast between before and after.
